title: Slack: compact context bundle formatting + per-incident rate limiting
author: Jacob Stein
description:
Problem: The context bundle is useful, but early responders reported the bot output is hard to scan in Slack and can spam incident threads when collectors retry or multiple alerts land in a short window. This PR improves readability (compact blocks, consistent timestamps, and collapsing noisy/empty sections) and adds bounded rate limiting keyed by incident+thread to keep the bot “fail-open” without creating noise.

What changed (high level): (1) Slack formatting: Standardized header + per-section blocks, consistent UTC timestamps + relative offsets, and more compact key/value rendering. Sections that have no data (or only "no changes") are collapsed behind a single-line summary. (2) Thread spam controls: Added per-incident rate limiting and de-duplication so the bot updates its most recent message when possible instead of posting a new reply. Rate limiter is conservative and fail-open: if limiter state store is unavailable, we still post, but we annotate that rate limiting is degraded.

Slack output changes: - Header now includes Incident ID, service, region(s), and "degradation window" start. - Each collector renders as a block with a short status line (OK / PARTIAL / ERROR) and a max of N lines before collapsing. - All timestamps are rendered as `2025-02-07T21:14:03Z (t-6m)` to avoid local-time confusion.

Rate limiting behavior: - Default: at most 1 context bundle post per incident thread per 90s (configurable). - De-dupe: if the bundle hash matches the last posted bundle (per collector section hashes), skip posting and add a debug log line. - Update-in-place: if Slack permits (message still editable + we have message_ts), we "chat.update" the most recent bundle message rather than adding a new reply.

Security/visibility notes: - No change to content redaction rules (handled in collectors). - New formatting code explicitly avoids printing raw JSON blobs by default; any structured fields are summarized and truncated.

Testing: - Added golden snapshot tests for Slack blocks (compact + collapsed variants). - Added rate-limiter unit tests (burst, de-dupe, store unavailable fallback). - Manual verification in #incidents-playground with recorded fixtures.

Follow-ups: - After merge, we should tune the default rate-limit window with on-call feedback (likely 60–120s depending on alert volume). - If responders want it, we can add an on-demand “expand details” command to post the full uncollapsed sections (separate PR).

Screenshots (text-only excerpt): Before: multiple 50+ line replies with repeated timestamps. After: 1 reply with compact blocks, e.g.
`[Deploys] OK • 2 in last 60m (us-east)`
`- api-gateway @ 8c12f3a (canary 10%) • merged PR #18421 • 21:12Z (t-4m)`
`- router @ 1f92d0e (full) • rollback candidate • 20:58Z (t-18m)`
commits: slack: introduce BlockBuilder and compact key/value formatting
slack: normalize timestamps to RFC3339 UTC + relative offsets
slack: collapse empty/no-change sections behind one-line summaries
bot: add per-incident rate limiter + bundle de-dup hashing
bot: prefer message update in-thread when re-posting within window
tests: add golden snapshots for slack blocks + rate limiter unit tests
docs: update internal formatting guidance + debug knobs
conversation:
Sean Gallagher (review): The collapsed sections look good. Two asks: (1) Make sure the header always shows incident start time, not “now”, and (2) ensure we don’t post more than once per minute by default — responders complained about spam in #incidents.

Jacob Stein (author): Updated header to include degradation window start when present; falls back to incident created_at. Set default to 90s in defaults.ts and made it configurable via INCIDENT_BOT_RATE_LIMIT_WINDOW_SECS.

Rafael Mendes (review): On rate limiting: if we skip posting due to dedupe, can we log at debug (not info)? Info logs are already noisy during incidents.

Jacob Stein (author): Good call. Moved dedupe skip logging to debug and added a single info-level metric increment `incident_bot.posts_skipped_dedupe`.

Marissa Cole (review): Formatting: can we keep section ordering stable and ensure the first screen of Slack shows deploy/config/saturation in that order? Also request consistent label casing (e.g., “Deploys”, “Config diff”, “Saturation”).

Jacob Stein (author): Implemented fixed ordering (deploys -> config -> saturation -> links). Normalized section titles and added a small unit test asserting order.

Marcus Lin (security review): Please confirm we’re not printing raw config payloads when formatting “diffs”. Even if collectors redact, formatting utilities should still truncate long values and avoid JSON dumps.

Jacob Stein (author): Added a hard cap (512 chars) per value and a “prettySummary()” helper that refuses to render objects/arrays unless explicitly allowlisted (currently none). Added tests for truncation.

CI: Initial run failed due to snapshot mismatch after timestamp normalization; reran after updating golden files.

Approval: Sean approved after default window increased. Rafael approved after logging change. Marcus approved after truncation guard. Marissa approved after section ordering.

Merged via squash; release note added to CHANGELOG under “Incident bot: Slack output readability and spam controls.”
release_notes: Incident bot Slack output is now more readable (compact blocks, consistent UTC timestamps, collapsed noisy sections) and less spammy via per-incident rate limiting and de-duplication.
